chapter: Building the band, Ivie Anderson and touring
title: Playing with string bass versus tuba and rehearsing
summary: Greer says his style didn't change, and the small band rehearsed arrangements.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So at that time that was when the
string bass came to the band. How did you as a drummer, did you feel any differently when you wereplaying with the string bass as opposed to the tuba? Did it change the way you played?

No, no. I never changed my style, under no conditions, because we were just a small aggregation and we had everything arranged, you know, in fact, we were the first band -- small one, we were a small group that had things arranged. We had everything rehearsed and arranged and we never used a string bass down at the Kentucky Club. We never used it till we went to the Cotton Club -- had a larger band.
Did you all rehearse much in those days?

Oh, yeah, we always was -- at that time, all the bands had music publishing house, standards, they call them standards, you know, and we used to take the standards and switch them around, don't play that like everybody else. We rehearse and the guys, we'd give individual solos, come back and that's why our band sound like a big band, but we never had no bass, because in the Kentucky Club, you must realize there wasn't no room for a bass. The bandstand was so small, one of them back-in-the-hole things.
And wasn't no way in the world a bass player could play a -- have a bass player with our band.
